orientation: Each feature compares the memory-conditioned response with the response without memory and is signed so that larger values favour the memory-conditioned response.

features.name: HEAD
features.definition: Heading difference: number of headings in the memory-conditioned response minus that in the response without memory.

features.name: LEN
features.definition: Relative length: log ratio of response lengths, oriented from the memory-conditioned to the no-memory response.

features.name: REL
features.definition: Memory relevance: relevance of the retrieved memories to the current query, scored without viewing either response.

features.name: PROP
features.definition: Assumption proportionality: whether personal assumptions are justified by the available memory evidence, compared between responses.

features.name: ASSUMP
features.definition: Unwarranted personal assumptions: degree to which a response assumes more about the user than the query establishes, compared between responses.

features.name: CLOSURE
features.definition: Actionable closure: whether a response supplies a clear next action rather than only considerations to weigh, compared between responses.

features.name: AXIS
features.definition: Advisory orientation: relative density of advisory versus factual language, (advisory - factual) / (advisory + factual), averaged across both responses.

features.name: COMMIT
features.definition: Recommendation commitment: commitment to a recommendation rather than enumeration of alternatives, compared between responses.

features.name: OPT
features.definition: Option framing: density of options and trade-off language, averaged across both responses.

features.name: BREADTH
features.definition: Coverage breadth: breadth of the information and alternatives covered, compared between responses.

features.name: COST
features.definition: Cost to first use: effort required before the user can act on an answer, compared between responses.

features.name: REGISTER
features.definition: Register fit: appropriateness of the response's language and register for the request, compared between responses.
